prerequisites: Linear Algebra: vector and matrix calculus.
Calculus and Advanced Calculus: operations with derivatives, integrals and solving differential equations.
Mechanics and Thermodynamics: fundamentals of kinematics, dynamics and energy transfer.
Strength of Materials: basic concepts of stress and strain.

learning_outcomes.text: Apply the principles of Fluid Mechanics to solve problems in the field of Engineering, evaluating and adopting reasonable simplifications in each situation.
Interpret the different variables of the fluid field and analyze the state of fluid-mechanical processes based on the values of these variables.
Design, calculate, model, analyze and interpret the operation of hydraulic systems.
Understand and mathematically express the physical principles of Fluid Mechanics (RMF-1).
Apply the principles of Fluid Mechanics to solve problems in the field of Engineering, evaluating and adopting reasonable simplifications in each situation (RMF-2).
Interpret the variables of the fluid field and analyze the state of fluid dynamic processes from their values (RMF-3).
Calculate, design and interpret the operation of fluid flow systems, in particular pipe and channel transport systems (RMF-4).
Design, create physical and numerical models, and analyze systems with fluid flow (RMF-5).

syllabus_topics: Conservation equations: differential and integral formulation
Introduction to fluid machines and drive systems
assessment_rules: For the ordinary assessment, the final grade is calculated as 0.75 x EF + 0.05 x AP + 0.10 x EP + 0.10 x C. A minimum score of 3.5 out of 10 in the final exam is required; if this minimum is not met, the final grade will be capped at 3.5. Attendance to a minimum of 5 out of 7 practice sessions is mandatory to take the laboratory exam. For the extraordinary assessment, the criteria are the same; if no complementary activities were completed, the final exam accounts for 75% and a minimum of 6.7 out of 10 is needed to pass. For differentiated evaluation, a written exam accounts for 90% and a methodological test (lab practices and other activities) for the remaining 10%.
